facts.raw_span: bilateral photophobia and decreased vision
CD4 count was 24 cells/mm3
HIV RNA level was 175,000 copies/mL
pruritic back rash of crusting erythematous plaques
presenting uncorrected visual acuity was hand motions in both eyes
intraocular pressures were 14 and 9 mm Hg in the right and left eye, respectively
corneal stromal haze, 3+ anterior chamber cell
vitreous cell and haze obscuring retinal vascular details
Cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay: positive
Rapid plasma reagin testing: 1:64 titer
interface dermatitis with spirochetes evident upon hematoxylin-eosin staining
Aqueous fluid from both eyes negative for herpetic viral DNA by PCR

concepts.why: Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing support syphilitic uveitis.
Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level suggest HIV-related immune recovery uveitis.
Negative aqueous fluid PCR for herpetic viral DNA and presence of vitreous cell and haze support toxoplasmic retinochoroiditis.
Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing support syphilitic retinitis.
Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level suggest cytomegalovirus retinitis.

concepts.preferred_label: Acute Posterior Multifocal Placoid Pigment Epitheliopathy
concepts.why: Negative aqueous fluid PCR for herpetic viral DNA and presence of vitreous cell and haze support APMPPE.
Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing support syphilitic chorioretinitis.
Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level suggest HIV-related progressive outer retinal necrosis.

rationales.F01: Bilateral photophobia and decreased vision are common symptoms of uveitis, which is consistent with Syphilitic Uveitis and Syphilitic Retinitis.
rationales.F04: A pruritic back rash of crusting erythematous plaques is a characteristic skin manifestation of secondary syphilis, which is consistent with Syphilitic Uveitis and Syphilitic Retinitis.
rationales.F09: A positive Cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay is a specific test for neurosyphilis, which is consistent with Syphilitic Uveitis and Syphilitic Retinitis.
rationales.F10: A positive Rapid plasma reagin test is a non-specific test for syphilis, but in the context of other symptoms, it supports the diagnosis of Syphilitic Uveitis and Syphilitic Retinitis.
rationales.F11: The presence of spirochetes in skin lesions is diagnostic of syphilis, which is consistent with Syphilitic Uveitis and Syphilitic Retinitis.
